headline: Road salt contract for 2027 recommended to full council at $74.37 per ton from New England Salt Company.
summary: The bid covers 10,200 tons of road salt, with Bangor's share at 8,000 tons. Brewer's public works director ran the bid, and the award goes to full council because of its amount. Police mobile data terminals moved forward on a 4-1 vote. Five other purchases, contracts, or grants also got votes.
decisions: Approved the bid from EdgePro Flooring to replace the Grand Ballroom carpet at the Cross Center.
Approved the 1/2 ton hybrid truck for code enforcement from Quirk Auto of Augusta, 5-0.
Approved moving forward with mobile data terminals for the police department, RhinoTab M4-17, on a 4-1 vote.
Recommended awarding the fiscal year '27 road salt contract to New England Salt Company at $74.37 per ton, 5-0.
Recommended that full council approve the bid from Global Ground Support for the airport deicer, 5-0.
Recommended the Mount Hope Avenue sidewalk project go to R.F. Jordan and Sons of Ellsworth, 5-0.
Recommended that full council authorize the city manager to accept and appropriate $3 million in Maine Department of Health and Human Services grant funds for the WIC program, 5-0.
discussion: Ballroom carpet bid: Questions covered whether a bid well under the $200,000 budgeted was typical. The vendor had not been used by the city before, and its references were described as strong.
Truck bid details: Questions covered whether Quirk Auto's bid price included a $500 document fee, since bids are taken as one all-in price. A revised bid form is to come back for council review.

Mobile data terminals sole source: A concern was raised about being tied to one vendor. The police lieutenant estimated staying with Patrol PC avoids about $30,000 in vehicle retrofits, and said its $163,000 bid was lower than Getac's $193,000 and Transcore's $260,000.

WIC grant reach: Questions covered how much of the program is in Bangor. The program serves the Penquis Public Health District, and 2,648 of its 4,492 participants have come to the Bangor clinic, though that does not mean all are Bangor residents.
